data.narrative:
Atmo is a Series A AI & Software company founded by Alex Levy and Johan Mathe, having raised $29.1M to date. The valuation framework draws from a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Palantir), spanning companies at Series A and Series B stages including Scale AI ($29.0B), Reflection AI ($25.0B), Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), and Black Forest Labs ($3.2B).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy valuation input, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $58M. Peer-median analysis across the 4-peer subset produces $15.3B, reflecting the distribution between $3.2B (floor) and $29.0B (ceiling). These methods reflect the substantial variance in frontier-tech valuations at this stage, where comparable companies span a wide valuation range.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $49M (low) to $17.6B (high), with a median indication of $7.7B. The extreme width of this range—spanning two orders of magnitude—underscores the primary uncertainty: appropriate peer-to-target scaling in a sector where stage-based advancement metrics diverge sharply from public-market multiples. Stage-progression suggests lower valuations; peer comparison suggests substantially higher. The final valuation will depend heavily on evidence of product-market fit and revenue traction relative to the selected peer cohort.
